correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the uniform two-fold energy balance and the multiplier, including the local uniqueness argument for a fixed neighborhood. Write δ=r−1 and ε=λ+(δ_+)^{3/2}. On a fixed time interval containing one harmonic turn, a bootstrap assuming state error at most Kε bounds the integral of |H(x)| by O((δ_++Kε)^{3/2}); Duhamel closes at O(ε) for fixed b and small parameters by first choosing K large and then shrinking the neighborhood. The return time is 2π+O(ε) by transversality. Replacing x by r sin t in the loss incurs O(ε√(δ_++ε)), since the integrand is locally Lipschitz and the union of active windows has that support scale. The harmonic loss is (8√2/3)(δ_+)^{3/2}+o((δ_+)^{3/2}); the input is (π+o(1))λ. The replacement error is o(λ+(δ_+)^{3/2}); this excludes fixed points with δ≤0 or outside a compact positive range of δ/λ^{2/3} as r→1. At λ=0, points a fixed distance above 1 lose energy, and points a fixed distance below 1 remain in the linear zone during a first return for small λ and have strictly positive displacement for λ>0. Nearby cycles cross the section, since the polar angle is strictly rotating on a sufficiently small annulus. The scaled displacement has one simple limiting zero C_b, with opposite signs on either side. The transverse-fold residence time is 4√(2δ)+o(√δ) by comparison of the contact windows; continuity of the field makes the matching variational saltation matrices identity. Liouville with section factor r/P(r) gives P′<1 on the compact scaled interval, uniqueness there, and at the fixed point log m=−4√2 b√C_b λ^{1/3}+o(λ^{1/3}). The uniform O(λ) trajectory comparison on this interval gives the same leading law for the maximum of |x|. No numerical estimate is needed for any of these limits.
residual_risks: The supplied numerical script checks section radius, not numerical Floquet contraction or maximum |x|. Its label for the multiplier constant follows an assignment, not a numerical test. These advertised diagnostics are not needed for the analytic validation.
The proof is for fixed b>0 and local uniqueness near the grazing circle; it gives no uniform joint-parameter claim.

value.rationale: This natural center-to-isolated-cycle transition has two distinct, measurable singular scales. The coefficients and uniform return law determine where the cycle sits and how weakly it attracts, data not supplied by a cycle count or by a grazing exponent alone. The model gives a reproducible benchmark for leading-order treatment of a pair of folds without claiming broad bifurcation or uniqueness results.
residual_risks: Scientific value is specific to the quantitative law, not to existence alone or an abstract first occurrence of fractional powers.
